short: Titus's five-month siege destroyed the Second Temple and broke the Judaean revolt.
full:
From around April 70 CE, Titus surrounded Jerusalem with four legions during Passover, when the city was swollen with pilgrims and divided between rival rebel factions under John of Gischala and Simon bar Giora. Roman forces breached the outer and second walls within weeks, but the Antonia Fortress and the Temple Mount held out through a summer of starvation, internal massacre and repeated Roman assaults recorded in detail by the eyewitness historian Josephus.

The Temple burned in late August or early September, whether by deliberate order or in the chaos of the final assault, and the Upper City fell soon after. Titus had the city and Temple razed, its treasures carried to Rome for his triumph and later displayed on the Arch of Titus. The destruction ended Temple Judaism's sacrificial cult and accelerated the shift of Jewish religious authority toward rabbinic scholarship centred on texts rather than the Temple.
